name: Psychiatry
tag: Visit length, inpatient/outpatient mix, no-shows, telehealth, call, APP supervision, interventional services.
questions: What are visit lengths for new/follow-up patients?

samples.name: Outpatient Psychiatry Group
samples.cons: No-show protection, APP oversight, and call must be clarified.

samples.name: Hospital Psychiatry Position
samples.cons: Consult/inpatient call and weekend burden could be heavy.

samples.name: Telepsychiatry Role
samples.cons: License burden, no-shows, telehealth restrictions, and panel ownership.

Compensation: Is pay salary, RVU, collections, session-based, call stipend, or hybrid?
Are telehealth visits reimbursed the same?
Is crisis coverage, inpatient call, or consult work paid separately?
Are TMS, ECT, ketamine/esketamine, or MAT services compensated differently?
Clinical model: What are visit lengths for new evaluations and follow-ups?
What therapy, social work, case management, and nursing support exists?
Who handles refills, prior authorizations, portal messages, and controlled-substance monitoring?
APP supervision: How many psych NPs/PAs are supervised?
Is supervision compensated by stipend, per visit, percent collections, or RVU credit?
Who owns liability for controlled substances, crisis calls, refills, and chart review?
Are APP panels independent or under physician oversight?
Quality bonus: Are metrics tied to access, PHQ/GAD documentation, hospitalization follow-up, patient satisfaction, safety planning, or medication monitoring?
What is max bonus and historical average payout?
Are metrics adjusted for acuity, no-shows, and staffing?
Lifestyle / call: What is after-hours call and crisis responsibility?
How are no-shows handled in schedule and compensation?
Contract risk: What is the noncompete and does it restrict telehealth?
Who owns patient panels if I leave?
Are there restrictions on outside private practice, moonlighting, or telepsych?

Clinical Fit: Visit lengths, acuity, inpatient/outpatient/telehealth mix, and support match practice style.
Compensation Upside: No-shows, telehealth, call, APP supervision, and TMS/ECT/MAT are compensated fairly.
Lifestyle Fit: Call, crisis coverage, documentation, and remote flexibility are sustainable.
Risk Safety: Noncompete, panel ownership, tail, outside practice, and controlled-substance workflows are clear.
Strategic Fit: Niche services, telehealth, outpatient panel, and referral demand build long-term value.
Collaborative Fit: Therapists, social workers, case managers, APPs, and inpatient teams are aligned.
